statement: return FormsDict((c.key, c.value) for c in cookies.values())
cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-93 requires CRLF sequences to be used as special elements for injection, but the code simply parses cookies into a dictionary without using CRLF as delimiters or special markers

connection.evidence: HTTP_COOKIE environment variable is parsed by SimpleCookie and values are passed to FormsDict construction

diff_causality.evidence: The candidate line constructs the FormsDict from cookie values, but there is no evidence this creates CRLF injection vulnerability

security_control.required_control: CRLF sequence neutralization when CRLF is used as a special element
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-93 requires neutralization only when CRLF sequences are used as delimiters or special elements in the processing logic
existing_controls_checked: SimpleCookie parsing handles cookie format, FormsDict stores key-value pairs
security_control.deficiency_evidence: No evidence that CRLF sequences are treated as special elements requiring neutralization in this cookie parsing context

concrete_impact.evidence: No demonstrated path where CRLF sequences in cookie values could cause injection attacks through this code

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, cookie values would still be parsed by SimpleCookie but not exposed via the FormsDict property, but this doesn't relate to CRLF injection mechanisms.
contradicting_evidence: CWE-93 requires CRLF to be used as a special element/delimiter, but cookie parsing uses standard cookie format delimiters (semicolons, equals signs)
FormsDict construction simply stores key-value pairs without using CRLF as record separators
No evidence of CRLF-based injection vectors in the cookie parsing and storage mechanism
